title: Flatten Cluttered Subfolders in 10 Lines of Python
description: Stop digging through nested directories just to move files by hand. Use this 10-line Python script to flatten deeply nested folders into one destination.

beats.voice: Forty-two files trapped across nested subfolders, pulled into one folder instantly.
Stop clicking through layers of directories just to drag documents out by hand.
Pathlib searches every subfolder recursively with rglob and grabs only raw files.
Shutil moves each item into your flat directory, safely skipping existing files.
This basic script skips name collisions, so check for duplicate filenames before moving...

kit_code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""tool.py - Flatten nested directory structures safely.

Recursively scans a source folder and consolidates all files into a
single flat destination directory with conflict handling and dry-run mode.
"""

import argparse
import logging
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import sys


def setup_logging(verbose: bool) -> None:
    level = logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.INFO
    logging.basicConfig(level=level, format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s")


def resolve_collision(target: Path, mode: str) -> Path | None:
    """Handle destination filename collisions based on policy."""
    if not target.exists():
        return target
    if mode == "skip":
        return None
    if mode == "overwrite":
        return target
    if mode == "rename":
        stem = target.stem
        suffix = target.suffix
        counter = 1
        while True:
            candidate = target.with_name(f"{stem}_{counter}{suffix}")
            if not candidate.exists():
                return candidate
            counter += 1
    return None


def flatten_folders(
    src: Path,
    dst: Path,
    dry_run: bool = True,
    conflict: str = "rename",
    copy_only: bool = False,
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Traverse src recursively and relocate files to dst."""
    if not src.exists() or not src.is_dir():
        logging.error(f"Source folder does not exist: {src}")
        return 0, 0

    if not dry_run:
        dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    processed = 0
    skipped = 0

    for item in src.rglob("*"):
        if not item.is_file():
            continue

        # Prevent processing files already in dst if dst is inside src
        if dst in item.parents:
            continue

        destination_path = resolve_collision(dst / item.name, conflict)
        if destination_path is None:
            logging.warning(f"Skipping collision: {item.name}")
            skipped += 1
            continue

        action_verb = "Copying" if copy_only else "Moving"
        if dry_run:
            logging.info(f"[DRY-RUN] {action_verb} {item} -> {destination_path}")
        else:
            try:
                if copy_only:
                    shutil.copy2(item, destination_path)
                else:
                    shutil.move(item, destination_path)
                logging.debug(f"{action_verb} {item.name} -> {destination_path.name}")
            except (OSError, shutil.Error) as err:
                logging.error(f"Failed to transfer {item}: {err}")
                skipped += 1
                continue

        processed += 1

    return processed, skipped


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Flatten nested folders into a single clean directory."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--src", required=True, type=Path, help="Source nested folder"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dst", required=True, type=Path, help="Destination flat folder"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--execute",
        action="store_true",
        help="Apply changes to disk. Defaults to dry-run mode if omitted.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--copy",
        action="store_true",
        help="Copy files instead of moving them.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--conflict",
        choices=["rename", "skip", "overwrite"],
        default="rename",
        help="Collision strategy: rename (default), skip, or overwrite.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose output"
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()
    setup_logging(args.verbose)

    is_dry_run = not args.execute
    if is_dry_run:
        logging.info("Running in DRY-RUN mode. Pass --execute to make changes.")

    moved, skipped = flatten_folders(
        src=args.src,
        dst=args.dst,
        dry_run=is_dry_run,
        conflict=args.conflict,
        copy_only=args.copy,
    )

    status = "Dry-run complete" if is_dry_run else "Finished"
    logging.info(f"{status}: {moved} processed, {skipped} skipped.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
kit_readme:
SETUP
tool.py uses only the Python standard library (pathlib, shutil, argparse, logging).
No third-party package installations or virtual environments are required.
Run with Python 3.10 or higher:
    python tool.py --help

HOW IT WORKS
The script recursively traverses the specified source folder using pathlib.rglob('*').
For every file encountered, it checks whether a file with the same name already exists in the destination folder.
By default, it operates in safe DRY-RUN mode, printing planned moves without writing to disk.
When run with --execute, it transfers each file into the destination folder.
If a name collision occurs, tool.py can automatically append a numbered suffix (_1, _2), skip the file, or overwrite based on the --conflict parameter.

ADAPTING IT
- To copy files while preserving the original structure intact, pass the --copy flag.
- To skip files with duplicate names instead of auto-renaming, pass --conflict skip.
- To filter for specific extensions (e.g. only .pdf or .csv), edit the loop in flatten_folders() to inspect item.suffix.

LIMITATIONS
- Large file moves across different physical disk drives or network mounts will execute as copy-then-delete, which takes longer than same-drive moves.
- If destination sits inside source, passing custom paths requires verifying you do not re-scan the destination folder.

SUPPORT
Provided as-is without warranty. Always run in default dry-run mode to verify the output list before passing --execute.
